### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.files

### Neovim version

0.12.x

### Description

If I open mini.files (from "tab 1") and open the selected file in a new tab (Using ctrl+t binding defined below), then I go back to "tab 1" from the newly opened "tab 2" and open mini.files again, instead of opening mini.files, it jumps back to the newly opened "tab 2" and doesn't open mini.files. However, if I open mini.files from "tab 2", it opens mini.files normally.

I followed the configuration examples that are found in `mini-files.txt`. The configuration looks like this. I'm only including this up front in case the issue is actually something to do with my configuration. There are other mini plugins installed but I assume those will not affect this configuration.

```lua
local MiniFiles = require("mini.files")
MiniFiles.setup()

local minifiles_toggle = function(...)
    if not MiniFiles.close() then
        MiniFiles.open(...)
    end
end

vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>ew", function()
    minifiles_toggle(nil, false)
end, { desc = "[E]xplore [W]orking Directory" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>ef", function()
    minifiles_toggle(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0), false)
end, { desc = "[E]xplore [F]iles" })

local mini_files_group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("mini_files", { clear = true })

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
    desc = "Show line numbers File Explorer",
    pattern = "MiniFilesWindowUpdate",
    group = mini_files_group,
    callback = function(args)
        local win_id = args.data.win_id
        vim.wo[win_id].number = true
        vim.wo[win_id].relativenumber = true
    end,
})

-- Define mapping for splitting into files.
local map_split = function(buf_id, lhs, direction)
    local rhs = function()
        -- Make new window and set it as target
        local cur_target = MiniFiles.get_explorer_state().target_window
        local new_target = vim.api.nvim_win_call(cur_target, function()
            vim.cmd(direction .. " split")
            return vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
        end)

        MiniFiles.set_target_window(new_target)
        MiniFiles.go_in()
    end

    local desc = "Split " .. direction
    vim.keymap.set("n", lhs, rhs, { buffer = buf_id, desc = desc })
end

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
    desc = "Bindings for splitting on file open",
    pattern = "MiniFilesBufferCreate",
    group = mini_files_group,
    callback = function(args)
        local buf_id = args.data.buf_id
        -- Tweak keys to your liking
        map_split(buf_id, "<C-s>", "belowright horizontal")
        map_split(buf_id, "<C-v>", "belowright vertical")
        map_split(buf_id, "<C-t>", "tab")
    end,
})
```

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    -- Add extra setup steps needed to reproduce the behavior
    -- Use `MiniDeps.add('user/repo')` to install another plugin from GitHub
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4.
- Copy the configuration from the above description below the provided content of `nvim-repro/init.lua` and restart neovim.
- Input `<leader>ef` to open mini.files with the provided keybind (since leader key is not set in the provided config, use default leader `\`).
- Select any file and input `<C-t>`. This will open the file in a new tab.
- Input `q`. The new tab should now be visible.
- Input `gt` to go back to the first tab.
- Input `<leader>ef` to open mini.files again.

### The problem
Here I would expect mini.files to open properly, instead it jumps back to the newly opened tab. Interestingly, this only happens if the new tab is opened via mini.files. If you instead open a new tab with any other method (using `<C-t>` in fzf-lua for example) and jump back to the original tab and open mini.files, it opens as expected. This problem only occurs when opening a split from mini.files.

### What I've tried
I thought maybe it had something to do with how mini.files handles the saving of the "previous" state so you can see that I adjusted my keymaps to set `{use_latest}` to false. This unfortunately did not fix the issue.

I am a new dev that's trying to gain additional experience, so I welcome to opportunity to try to fix this on my own, but I would definitely appreciate some pointers on how to get started as well as some patience for any future questions I might have. I also welcome criticism of the results I produce to help me improve. 

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body: For future reference for myself, is there a way that I can add the mini.files label myself? I couldn't see how to do it when I was creating the issue.

Thanks for the issue!

I indeed can reproduce. *But* for the future I highly recommend trimming down the reproduction config to contain as minimum amount of code as possible to reproduce the issue. Otherwise it will be a maintainer's job when they will try figure out what is going on. Many people in other projects will straight up close the issue if it contains too many unnecessary steps.

For example:
- The autocommand that adds line numbers is not relevant to the issue.
- Opening an explorer via a "toggle" keymap is technically not relevant to the issue as it is described ("Opening 'mini.files' after split ..."). However, when actually trying to minimize the config, it reveals that it is related and actually the main culprit to the behavior described here. Because executing `:=MiniFiles.close()` instead of typing `<Leader>ef` as the last step shows that it returns `true` (i.e. something was closed) when it should return `false`. It also changes the tabpage.

> For future reference for myself, is there a way that I can add the mini.files label myself? I couldn't see how to do it when I was creating the issue.

Adding labels is something that only people with specific access to the repository can do. For other people this project asks to select from a drop-down list of modules.
This should now be resolved on the latest `main`.

title: [mini.files] Opening mini.files after split to tab breaks future opens
